title: The Blessing of Living Under Authority
author: Michael Foster
summary: Michael Foster argues that a Christian household must teach that everyone lives under authority, and that rejecting this is the root of many social and spiritual problems. He starts with the centurion in Matthew 8 and Luke 7, who understood that he stood between those above and below him and therefore trusted Christ as a benevolent authority. He then reads Genesis as a reversal of the flow of authority, in which the serpent persuades people to distrust those God has placed over them. Abusive authorities exist, he concedes, but the abuse of a good thing is not grounds for rejecting its right use. Turning to the home, he uses Ephesians 6 and Hebrews 12 to argue that parents are middlemen under God and that loving discipline produces peaceful fruit. He closes by urging fathers, pastors and managers never to apologize for the authority they have been given.
points: Foster frames the home as the place where children learn that all people, parents included, are under authority, and sees failure here as the source of later social and spiritual disorder.
The centurion is offered as a model of trusting authority, someone who came with humble requests rather than demands as an entitled equal.
He reads the fall as a reversal of authority and argues that the modern assumption that authorities cannot be trusted continues that strategy.
Parents are middlemen who are themselves under God, elders and civil authority, so discipline is an act of love rather than a power trip.
He warns of ditches on both sides and calls proud disrespect for authority the deeper one, urging leaders at home, church and work not to apologize for their role.
quotes: You are designed to live under authority. And to rebel against this is to rebel against reality itself.

He wasn't a free-floating independent operator who was at liberty to do whatever he pleased. He was under certain immutable obligations to those above him, and likewise, those below him were under obligations to him.
In short, you have a reversal of the flow of authority in Satan's sly attack. And his stratagem has not changed. Get people under authority to distrust those whom God has put over them.
In other words, the abuse of a good thing is not grounds for the rejection of its right use.
Parents, not unlike the centurion, are middlemen. They are, at the very least, under the authority of the Lord.
Those who refuse to discipline those under their care sentence them to short-term pleasure and ease, followed by a life of pain and chaos.
Never apologize for it. Never be ashamed of it. Know that rebels will resent it, but if you use it rightly according to the Word of God, it will be a blessing to all those under your care.
